newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday with a domestic A share issue pushing up demand, traders said. The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract was little changed at 14.51 percent from 14.5 percent on Monday.
Total turnover fell to 11.29 million lots from 13.39 million on Monday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the issue of A share Jiamusi Papermaking Co Ltd on the Shenzhen exchange on Tuesday incresed demand and supported the rates, especially the early-maturing contracts.
The rate for the shortest three-day contract surged to 25 percent at the close from 14 percent as a result, they said.
Traders said the listing of three new A share companies on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges would keep rates at these high levels on Wednesday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Tuesday, continuing a technical correction which started on Monday, traders said.
The most active three-year note maturing in August 1999, a market barometer, bucked the trend to close up at 104.17 yuan from 104.10 yuan, indicating market sentiment was good.

Traders said the three-year note was supported by big institutions, particularly in late trading, and this indicated the spot market would end its technical correction and begin a rebound over the coming few days.
Combined volume of the nine-contract market fell to 1.2 million lots from 1.53 million.
